name: HubSpot
one_liner: HubSpot is a comprehensive CRM, marketing, sales, and customer service platform with extensive REST and GraphQL APIs and an official remote MCP server for managing CRM records, activities, content, and conversations.
auth_notes: Multi-account integrations must use OAuth2 (30-minute Bearer access tokens with refresh tokens, plus PKCE required for the remote MCP server at mcp.hubspot.com and client_credentials supported for the webhooks journal API); single-account integrations can use static app access tokens or scoped service keys (pat-*) as Bearer tokens, while select app features require a developer API key.
access_notes: Developers can self-serve create apps, OAuth credentials, service keys, and MCP connectors, with Free and Starter tiers supporting up to 250,000 API calls per account/day for privately distributed apps; however, private OAuth apps are capped at 10 accounts, wider distribution requires Marketplace distribution, API availability and rate limits vary by HubSpot product and subscription tier (e.g., Revenue Hub Professional/Enterprise for revenue objects), and governed agentic features consume HubSpot Credits.
api_surface_notes: Covers core CRM objects (contacts, companies, deals, tickets, leads, line items, products, appointments, courses, listings, projects, services, custom objects), CRM Search, Associations, GraphQL API, webhooks, and revenue objects on eligible plans; accounts have a combined limit of 100 project-based apps, service keys, and MCP connectors.
verification_changes: api_protocol: REST -> REST + GraphQL (The official API usage guidelines and limits page (https://developers.hubspot.com/docs/developer-tooling/platform/usage-guidelines) explicitly documents a GraphQL API alongside HubSpot's REST APIs.)

name: DealCloud
one_liner: DealCloud is an enterprise CRM and relationship/pipeline management platform with REST APIs and an official MCP server for reading and updating deal data.
auth_notes: REST API uses OAuth2 Client Credentials (client_id and user API key as client_secret) to mint 15-minute Bearer tokens; the official MCP server uses OAuth 2.0 with .well-known dynamic discovery.
access_notes: No self-serve developer sandbox or free trial; requires an enterprise DealCloud customer tenant (and Celeste license for MCP), admin or CSM permissioning for API keys, and Account Manager approval for third-party or custom MCP clients.
api_surface_notes: REST APIs cover Data and Schema (v4), User Management (v1), Publications (v1), Relationship Intelligence Import (v1), and Site Backups (v4), with per-tenant Swagger endpoints; rate limits are not detailed in the retrieved docs.
primary_blocker: No self-serve developer sandbox; requires enterprise DealCloud tenant/partner access and Account Manager approval for third-party MCP integrations.

name: WhatsApp Business
one_liner: Enables businesses to programmatically send and receive WhatsApp messages, manage message templates, onboard phone numbers, and handle customer communications at scale via Meta's WhatsApp Business Platform.
auth_notes: Uses Meta Business Portfolio access tokens and permissions (`whatsapp_business_messaging`, `whatsapp_business_management`, `whatsapp_business_manage_events`) with Admin/Employee System Users for production API calls, Embedded Signup for Solution Partners, and Meta developer account OAuth (`business_management`, `whatsapp_business_management`, `whatsapp_business_messaging`) for the official WhatsApp Business Tools MCP server.
access_notes: Developers can self-serve register in Meta App Dashboard, create a Business Portfolio, connect a Messaging account and WhatsApp account, and accept Cloud API Terms of Service. Solution Partners and multi-tenant integrations require App Review for Advanced Access permissions, business verification improves throughput, and message delivery beyond the free entry point or 1,000 monthly free service messages requires a payment method in Billing Hub.
api_surface_notes: Built on Meta's Graph API (Cloud API and Marketing Messages API), covering template and non-template messaging, media, phone number onboarding and verification, message template management, business profiles, webhook configuration, and conversion event logging. Non-template messages are restricted to an open 24-hour customer service window, while template messages require approval and user opt-in.
primary_blocker: Production and multi-tenant usage require a Meta Business Portfolio with separate WhatsApp and Messaging accounts, Cloud API Terms of Service acceptance, App Review for Advanced Access permissions, template approvals, Billing Hub payment setup, and adherence to the 24-hour customer service window.

name: Sherlock
one_liner: Sherlock is an open-source CLI tool and Python library for hunting down social media accounts by username across hundreds of public websites and social networks.
auth_notes: Requires no API keys, accounts, or credentials; runs locally by sending direct HTTP requests to publicly accessible profile URLs (with optional proxy support).
access_notes: MIT-licensed open-source Python package (sherlock-project) installed via pipx, pip, uv, or Docker. A third-party Apify Cloud Actor exists for remote execution, which requires an Apify account and API token.
api_surface_notes: No official hosted web API exists; exposes a local CLI and Python sherlock(username, site_data, query_notify, ...) function querying a JSON site manifest. An experimental Django REST Framework repo (sherlock-project/api) requires local self-hosting and has been unmaintained since 2021.
primary_blocker: No hosted public web API; Sherlock is a local CLI and Python scraping/probing library with only an unmaintained self-hosted DRF repo and third-party Apify wrapper.

name: Otter AI
one_liner: Otter AI is an AI meeting transcription and conversation intelligence platform offering a Public REST API for Enterprise workspaces and an official hosted MCP server for querying transcripts.
auth_notes: Split auth model: the Public REST API uses static Bearer API keys generated in Integrations > Developer (max 2 keys per user, no OAuth), whereas the official hosted MCP server (https://mcp.otter.ai/mcp) uses OAuth browser consent with per-meeting granular permissions and no public API key support.
access_notes: The Public REST API and Super Admin APIs are strictly gated to custom-priced Enterprise workspaces (requiring an Enterprise contract and contacting an Otter account manager to enable). In contrast, the read-only hosted MCP server is available on all plans including the free Basic plan via OAuth.
api_surface_notes: REST API (https://api.otter.ai/v1, 10 req/s rate limit, cursor pagination) covers channels, channel members, conversations, transcripts, audio, action items, insights, outlines, and Super Admin workspace endpoints. Official MCP exposes 3 read-only tools: get user info, search, and fetch.
primary_blocker: The Public REST API is Enterprise-only (account-manager gated) and lacks OAuth, requiring each end user to manually provision static Bearer API keys; only the narrow 3-tool read-only official MCP server supports self-serve OAuth for standard accounts.
